title: The normalization of a scheme in a finite extension of a residue field is a normal integral scheme, integral over the base, with the extension as generic point
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $x\in X$ a point with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field], $K/\kappa(x)$ a finite field extension, and $h:\operatorname{Spec}K	o\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)	o X$ the composite of the induced morphism with the canonical morphism [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and there are a scheme $Y$, an integral morphism $
u:Y	o X$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and a morphism $g:\operatorname{Spec}K	o Y$ with $h=
u\circ g$ such that: (a) $Y$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] all of whose local rings $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ are integrally closed domains (Y is normal); (b) $g$ maps the point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to the generic point $\eta_Y$ of $Y$ and induces an isomorphism $\kappa(\eta_Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ of fields, i.e. $g$ is the inclusion of the generic point of $Y$ with $K$ as function field. (One may take for $
u$ the normalization of $X$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$, Stacks 035H: $Y=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_X(\mathcal O')$ with $\mathcal O'$ the integral closure of $\mathcal O_X$ in $h_*\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}K}$; if $Z\subseteq X$ is the reduced closed subscheme on $\overline{\{x\}}$, it is also the normalization of $Z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$, by the last clause of Stacks 035I, which is the scheme used in the proof of Stacks 09Z6.)

Y is a normal integral scheme ... it is clear that K is the function field of Y'; the function-field identification is called clear there)

proof.text: *$h$ is qcqs.* $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and $X$ is quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (1) (a morphism from a quasi-compact scheme to a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-compact; a morphism from a quasi-separated scheme is quasi-separated) $h:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. So the normalization of $X$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is defined.

source.place: Lemma 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence) and Lemma 01KV (lemma-compose-after-separated), applied with T -> Spec Z, as in the last paragraph of the proof of Morphisms Lemma 035I

proof.text:
*The normalization; $Y$ integral.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] to $f=h$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$: we get $Y:=X'$, $
u:Y	o X$ and $g:=f':\operatorname{Spec}K	o Y$ with $h=
u\circ g$, $
u$ integral (i), $g$ dominant (ii), and the affine description (iii). $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] (it is nonempty and its only nonempty open is the whole space, with ring $K$, a domain), so $Y$ is integral by (iv). (Stacks 09Z6 normalizes the reduced closure $Z$ of $x$ instead; by the last clause of Morphisms 035I applied to the integral morphism $Z	o X$ through which $h$ factors, the normalization of $Z$ in $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is the same $X$-scheme, so nothing changes; working over $X$ avoids $Z$.)

source.place: Definition 035H (line 13910), Lemma 035I (line 13936), Lemma 0AXN (line 14067); literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex proof of Lemma 09Z6, lines 12967-12975

proof.text:
*The ring of $Y$ over an affine open.* Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open, $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$. The set $h^{-1}(U)$ is open in the one-point space $\operatorname{Spec}K$, so it is empty if $x
otin U$ and all of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ if $x\in U$. If $x
otin U$, then $B=\Gamma(h^{-1}(U),\mathcal O)=0$, its integral closure $A'_U$ is $0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] (iii) $
u^{-1}(U)$ is the affine scheme with ring $0$, i.e. $
u^{-1}(U)=\emptyset$. If $x\in U$, let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ be the prime corresponding to $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (2) the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)	o X$ factors through $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ via the ring map $A	o\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(x)$, so by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] the map $h^\sharp:A	o\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}K,\mathcal O)=K$ is $\psi:A	o\kappa(\mathfrak p)	o K$, whose kernel is $\mathfrak p$ (a map of fields is injective; [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (1)). Put $A_0=A/\mathfrak p$, a domain with fraction field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ ([lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (1)); $\psi$ induces $A_0\subseteq\kappa(\mathfrak p)\subseteq K$. An element $k\in K$ is integral over $A$ (via $\psi$) iff it is integral over $A_0$: a monic equation over $A$ maps to one over $A_0$, and a monic equation over $A_0$ lifts coefficientwise to one over $A$ with the same value at $k$, since $A$ acts on $K$ through $A_0$. So $A'_U$ = the integral closure of $A$ in $K$ = the integral closure of $A_0$ in $K$. As $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{Frac}(A_0)$, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] gives: $A'_U$ is a normal domain and $K$ is a fraction field of $A'_U$ via the inclusion $A'_U\subseteq K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] (iii), $
u^{-1}(U)$ is affine with $\Gamma(
u^{-1}(U),\mathcal O_Y)\cong A'_U$, under which $g^\sharp$ on $
u^{-1}(U)$ is the inclusion $A'_U\subseteq K$.

proof.text:
*$Y$ is normal.* $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is an integral scheme (step 2) whose only local ring is $K$ (the localization of $K$ at its zero ideal), a field, hence an integrally closed domain; $h$ is qcqs (step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-normal-stalks] every local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is an integrally closed domain. (Concretely, by step 3: every $y\in Y$ lies in $
u^{-1}(U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A'_U$ for an affine open $U
i
u(y)$, necessarily with $x\in U$, and $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is a localization of the normal domain $A'_U$.)

proof.text: *$g$ hits the generic point.* Let $\xi$ be the point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. $Y$ is integral (step 2), so irreducible, with a unique generic point $\eta_Y$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. Since $g$ is dominant (step 2), $\overline{\{g(\xi)\}}=\overline{g(\operatorname{Spec}K)}=Y$, so $g(\xi)$ is a generic point of the irreducible closed set $Y$, and $g(\xi)=\eta_Y$ by uniqueness.

source.place: Lemma 035I (f' dominant), Lemma 035L ('Y -> X' is dominant'); Schemes Lemma 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober)

proof.text:
*The function field is $K$.* Choose an affine open $U\subseteq X$ containing $x$. Then $
u(\eta_Y)=
u(g(\xi))=h(\xi)=x\in U$, so $\eta_Y\in V:=
u^{-1}(U)$, and $g^{-1}(V)=h^{-1}(U)=\operatorname{Spec}K$. By step 3, $V$ is affine with ring $A'_U$, and the restriction $g:\operatorname{Spec}K	o V$ corresponds ([lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]) to the inclusion $\iota:A'_U\subseteq K$, which is injective with $K$ a fraction field of the domain $A'_U$ (step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] (3), $g(\xi)$ is the generic point $(0)$ of $V=\operatorname{Spec}A'_U$ and the induced map of residue fields $\kappa_V(\eta_Y)	o K$ is an isomorphism. As $V$ is open in $Y$, $\mathcal O_{V,\eta_Y}=\mathcal O_{Y,\eta_Y}$, so $\kappa(\eta_Y)	o K$ induced by $g$ is an isomorphism: $g$ is the inclusion of the generic point of $Y$ and $K$ is the function field of $Y$. This proves (b), and (a) is steps 2 and 4.

lean.statement: theorem normalization_in_finite_residue_field_extension (X : Scheme.{u}) [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (x : X) (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra (X.residueField x) K] [Module.Finite (X.residueField x) K] : QuasiCompact (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K)) ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x) ∧ QuasiSeparated (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K)) ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x) ∧ ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (ν : Y ⟶ X) (g : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Y), IsIntegralHom ν ∧ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap (X.residueField x) K)) ≫ X.fromSpecResidueField x = g ≫ ν ∧ IsIntegral Y ∧ (∀ y : Y, IsDomain (Y.presheaf.stalk y) ∧ IsIntegrallyClosed (Y.presheaf.stalk y)) ∧ ∃ η : Y, IsGenericPoint η Set.univ ∧ g (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = η ∧ IsIso (g.residueFieldMap (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K))
